subject: Elara5b: intermittent 5xx/timeouts — update & recovery plan
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lopez <tara@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Elara5b: intermittent 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Hi Tara —

Quick heads-up: starting ~07:45 PDT we observed an increase in 5xx responses and timeout errors for requests routed to the Elara5b model serving pool that you use for StellarNet's summarization endpoint. Impact is intermittent (spikes at ~10–15% of requests over 5m windows) and affects long-context workloads (>= 3k token prefixes) the most.

What we know so far:
- Scope: Elara5b serving pool in us-west-2, several customers impacted; StellarNet traffic shows elevated 5xx and rare client-side timeouts.
- Symptom: unhandled inference exceptions and occasional RPC timeouts; retries sometimes succeed.
- Initial mitigation: routing policy enacted to move new traffic to a warmed Elara5b fallback pool and to a smaller Elara-lite variant for long-prefix requests.

Immediate ask from our side: can you confirm whether you have any large batch jobs (bulk re-indexing or backfills) running right now that might increase long-prefix concurrency? That will help us prioritize routing.

We're treating this as high priority — engineers are triaging kernel and KV cache behavior now. I'll update you within the hour with timeline and next steps.

Attachments: [Attachment: incident_logs_0601.txt (txt, 42KB)]

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

We saw errors starting ~07:50 PDT with about ~12% of summarize requests failing or timing out. If a fallback model is safe, we can opt-in.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Elara5b triage notes and proposed mitigations

Priya / team — quick internal summary of what ops has found so far: 
- Repro: high-concurrency, long-prefix (3k+) sequences trigger a KV cache eviction race in the custom attention kernel for Elara5b when multiple streams touch the same key ranges — leads to null-pointer in the runtime and a 5xx.
- Frequency: appears under sustained concurrency > 120 streams per shard; triggers within ~2–6 minutes after the concurrency spike.
- Temporary mitigation applied at 08:25 PDT: conservative per-shard concurrency cap + prefix-aware routing to Elara-lite for long contexts. That reduced observed 5xx from ~15% to ~3% in canary shards.

Next steps (assignments):
- Karthik: push a hotfix to the attention kernel to add an atomic guard around KV eviction in the next 90 minutes (canary first).
- Michael: expand fallback routing rules and validate correctness for trace IDs so StellarNet sees consistent results.
- Priya: keep external comms and coordinate credit/SLAs with Tara.

We should plan a formal postmortem once kernel fix is validated.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lopez <tara@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Update: Elara5b mitigation and temporary recommendations

Hi Tara —

Short update after engineering triage: we identified a concurrency-related KV cache eviction race in the Elara5b attention kernel as the primary cause. Our immediate mitigations (already in place):
- Route long-context (>=3000 tokens) requests to Elara-lite automatically for StellarNet traffic.
- Apply a conservative concurrency cap per shard to reduce contention.
- Canary deploy of an atomic guard in the attention kernel is scheduled; we expect canary verification within ~60–90 minutes.

Recommended actions for StellarNet (optional but helpful):
- If possible, temporarily reduce max_tokens for summarization pipelines to 2k for the next 3–4 hours.
- Avoid large concurrent batch jobs until we confirm kernel canary is healthy.

Compensation and SLA: we will log this incident against your account for credit review and include the event in the postmortem.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/ELARA-20280601 (live updates)

I'll share a postmortem draft for your review by end of day tomorrow. Please let me know if you want a quick sync call.

Best,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lopez <tara@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-03T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem: Elara5b elevated 5xx/timeouts (June 1) — findings & actions

Tara / StellarNet team —

Thank you for your patience while we completed the investigation. Below is the concise postmortem and the actions we've taken. If you prefer a full formatted PDF, I've attached the draft postmortem (postmortem_draft_elara.pdf).

Incident summary (what happened):
- Between 07:45–10:45 PDT on 2028-06-01, Elara5b serving shards experienced intermittent 5xx responses and RPC timeouts affecting long-context requests. StellarNet observed ~10–15% failure rate at peak.

Root cause (technical):
- A race condition in the Elara5b attention kernel's KV cache eviction path caused stale pointer dereferences when multiple concurrent streams attempted overlapping KV updates. The race manifested under sustained concurrency (>120 streams/shard) with large prefix sequences.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Automated routing of long-context requests to Elara-lite and conservative per-shard concurrency caps (08:25 PDT).
- Kernel atomic guard hotfix deployed to canary (09:40 PDT) and rolled to production after validation (11:05 PDT).
- Expanded observability: added eviction counters, per-shard concurrency alarms, and trace-id linkability for debug.

Longer-term fixes and commitments:
- Engineering will harden the attention kernel with additional unit tests and stress tests for long-prefix concurrency (owner: Karthik). Target: complete by 2028-07-01.
- We will add a configurable customer-level policy to opt into Elara-lite for high prefix workloads to avoid surprises (owner: Michael). ETA: 2028-07-15.
- We will run a joint runbook review with StellarNet to validate failover behavior and preferences.

Customer impact & remediation:
- We logged the incident on your account and will apply a credit equivalent to the impacted usage window. Priya will follow up with a credit proposal via HubSpot.

Attachments and links:
- Postmortem draft attached: postmortem_draft_elara.pdf
- Incident log snapshot: incident_logs_0601.txt (attached earlier)
- Status/details: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/ELARA-20280601

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with Karthik and Michael this week to go over the kernel changes and the fallback routing.

Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability is critical and we appreciate the partnership while we resolve this.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
